newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 8.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--Some 30,000 civil servants are to get no increases in the government's new wage scale, calculated to be faithful to convergence programme targets and to keep reactions to the minimum.

--The bourse faces a credibility crisis as authorities find themselves incapable of the effective control of procedures. The inability of a leading brokerage firm to cover debts to the clearing house has endangered the interests of thousands of small investors and many brokerage firms.
--Greece is moving towards abolishing the ban on those owing the state leaving the country. A higher court ruling on the ban, which runs contrary to the Maastricht treaty, is expected soon.
--The national economy and defence ministries discover a 1.3 trillion drachma discrepancy between their proposals for the Greek armed forces' new armaments programme budget.
--A massive underwater operation is under way near the Aegean island of Samos to determine the reasons behind the sinking of the 'Kostakos' gunboat, which now lies at a depth of 150 metres.

--The main opposition New Democracy party yesterday took a step back from the chasm as leader Miltiades Evert agrees to hold the party's congress earlier than announced and his opponents back off on their call for new internal elections.

--Public servants on high wages are the losers in the government's new wage scale for the public service. The winners are teachers, healthcare workers and low wage earners. The union, ADEDY, however, says the scale does not meet its expectations.
--The bourse gets a fright as a leading brokerage firm finds itself unable to cover its obligations of 1.3 billion drachmas, as well as passing a bad cheque.

--New Democracy's deputy vice-president Ioannis Varvitsiotis finds himself in the unenviable position of refereeing the truce agreed yesterday between leader Miltiades Evert and would-be leader George Souflias and his supporters.
--Opposition Democratic Social Movement (DHKKI) leader and former PASOK finance minister Dimitris Tsovolas predicts the economy will go from bad to worse.
--The captain of the passenger ferry that rammed and sank the navy gunboat on Monday night refuses to take the blame for the accident.
--New Democracy gets some breathing space. Leader Evert remains at the helm but the congress will be held sooner than announced.
